authors.intro: Trent Horn is a staff apologist at Catholic Answers, which he joined in 2012, and the host of the weekly podcast The Counsel of Trent. He entered the Catholic Church at seventeen and went on to earn three master's degrees, in theology, philosophy, and bioethics. His books answer the objections of atheists and Protestants, work through difficult passages of Scripture, and make the pro-life case, with steady attention to charitable and persuasive conversation. All are in copyright, so we link to them.

authors.intro: Thomas E. Woods Jr. is an American historian who studied at Harvard and earned his doctorate at Columbia. He appears here for his books on Catholic history: How the Catholic Church Built Western Civilization, The Church Confronts Modernity, a study of Catholic intellectuals in the Progressive Era, and Sacred Then and Sacred Now, on the traditional Latin Mass. He also writes on economics and politics; in The Church and the Market he argues for a free economy. Those views are his own, not Church teaching.
authors.intro_note: The Church and the Market is described as his argument (from its subtitle), not as Catholic social teaching. No political label is used in the copy.

authors.intro: Scott Hahn, born in 1957, is a biblical theologian who has taught at Franciscan University of Steubenville since 1990 and founded the St. Paul Center for Biblical Theology. Ordained a Presbyterian minister in 1982, he entered the Catholic Church at the Easter Vigil of 1986, a journey he and his wife Kimberly tell in Rome Sweet Home. His popular books, including The Lamb's Supper and Hail, Holy Queen, explain the Mass and Mary through Scripture. All are in copyright, so we link to them.
authors.intro_note: The Mass and Mary come from the subtitles of The Lamb's Supper and Hail, Holy Queen (Open Library).

authors.intro: Warren H. Carroll (1932–2011) was an American historian who earned his doctorate at Columbia and was received into the Catholic Church in 1968. In 1977 he founded Christendom College in Virginia, serving as its first president and later chairing its history department until 2002. His multi-volume History of Christendom tells the story of the West from an openly Catholic perspective, and he also wrote on Isabel of Spain and Our Lady of Guadalupe. His books are in copyright, so we link to them.
